findings.title: Device limit is bypassed after the first rejected request
findings.description:
`tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (line 87) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (line 93). When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the key stays cached. The same device's next request hits the cache at line 83, returns `nil`, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` (`client.go:44-58`) issues an anonymous identity.

A device over the limit is therefore blocked for one request, then admitted for the cache lifetime (29 minutes, `impl.go:42`) on that instance. Set the cache entry only after the store call succeeds, or evict it on error.

findings.title: Limit is skipped entirely when the device ID header is absent
findings.description:
`TagDevice` returns `nil` when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is empty, and also when the IP fails to parse (lines 126-129). `Authenticate` then grants the anonymous identity without any limit check.

Any client that omits the header is never counted or limited. The reverse also holds: device IDs are client-supplied and unauthenticated, so one client can send `device_limit` random IDs and lock out every legitimate anonymous user for the 30-day window. If the limit is meant as an enforcement control, both gaps need a deliberate decision.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the limit can be exceeded
findings.description: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and the upsert in another, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. With tagging now on the request path and multiple instances in HA, this is a realistic race.

findings.title: Synchronous DB work added to the anonymous auth path
findings.description:
The background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout was replaced by an inline `TagDevice` call. Every anonymous request that misses the local cache now blocks on a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` plus an upsert or update before it can authenticate. This applies when `device_limit` is set; with the default of 0 only the upsert runs inline.

A slow or locked database now adds latency directly to anonymous page loads, whereas before it was invisible to the request. Consider running inline only when `deviceLimit > 0` and keeping the async path otherwise.

findings.title: `rowsAffected == 0` is reported as "device limit reached"
findings.description:
`updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever the `UPDATE` matches no rows. That covers a device that does not exist, but also one whose `updated_at` falls outside the `BETWEEN` window. The sentinel is then surfaced as an auth failure even though the cause may be unrelated to the limit.

The window is also anchored on `device.UpdatedAt` (line 81), while the count that gates this path uses `time.Now()` (line 110). The two predicates can disagree for callers passing a non-current `UpdatedAt`, as the new test does.

findings.title: Captured `args` slice is mutated inside a retryable callback
findings.description:
`args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` reassigns the captured outer variable inside the `WithDbSession` callback. `withDbSession` re-invokes the callback on SQLite `ErrLocked`/`ErrBusy` (`pkg/services/sqlstore/session.go:86-103, 127`).

On a retry the query string is prepended a second time, so `Exec` receives the SQL text as its first bind parameter and fails with an argument-count mismatch. The pattern is copied from the existing code at lines 149-151, but the new function repeats it; build a local slice inside the closure instead.

findings.title: Stale wire provider left behind with an unsatisfiable `int64` parameter
findings.description:
`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes `deviceLimit int64`, but it is still registered in the wire set along with its `AnonStore` binding. Nothing injects `anonstore.AnonStore` any more, since `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself.

The entries are dead wiring, and anything that later injects `AnonStore` will fail wire generation because no provider exists for `int64`. I did not run wire, so I cannot say whether it already complains. Remove the two lines, or have the provider take `*setting.Cfg`.

findings.title: Service now constructs its concrete store instead of receiving the interface
findings.description:
`ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` previously accepted `anonstore.AnonStore`; it now takes `db.DB` and calls `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` internally. This couples the service to the SQL implementation and makes `FakeAnonStore` unusable through the constructor.

The tests show the cost: `impl_test.go:124` now reaches into the private `anonService.anonStore` field. Passing `cfg` into `ProvideAnonDBStore` would deliver the limit without changing the service's dependency.

findings.title: Tests cover only the rejection path at the store level
findings.description:
`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` asserts only that a second device is rejected at limit 1. The following are untested:
- **Existing device at the limit:** it should still update successfully through the `updateDevice` success branch.
- **Auth client behaviour:** `Authenticate` should return an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and still succeed on other tagging errors. `client_test.go` was not updated, and `anontest.FakeService.TagDevice` always returns `nil`, ignoring its `ExpectedError` field.
- **Repeat request after rejection:** a service-level test of this would have caught the cache bypass in the FAIL finding.
- **Config parsing:** nothing covers `device_limit`.

findings.title: Frontend config property is typed as `undefined` and never matches the backend value
findings.description:
`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no annotation, so the class property's type is inferred from the initializer rather than `number | undefined`. Neighbouring fields use the explicit form, for example `loginError: string | undefined = undefined;` at line 85.

The backend DTO field is a non-pointer `int64` with no `omitempty` (`pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195`), so the frontend always receives a number, with `0` meaning no limit. Either type it as `number` defaulting to `0`, or make the DTO field optional so that `undefined` is a real state.

findings.title: New `device_limit` setting is not documented in the config files
findings.description: `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read here, but neither `conf/defaults.ini` (section at line 581) nor `conf/sample.ini` (section at line 570) declares it. Every other key in the section appears in both files. Negative values are also silently treated as "no limit" by the `> 0` check.

findings.title: Limit sentinel is a plain error, so the user gets a generic auth failure
findings.description:
`ErrDeviceLimitReached` is created with `fmt.Errorf` and no format verbs; `errors.New` is the idiomatic form. It carries no status code or public message.

`authnimpl.Service.Authenticate` joins it into the aggregate auth error (`pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/service.go:207`), so a rejected user sees a generic unauthenticated response rather than an explanation. An `errutil` error with a public message would make the rejection diagnosable.

findings.title: The 30-day window constant is now defined in several places
findings.description: `anonymousDeviceExpiration` is declared in both `anonstore/database.go:16` and `api/api.go:18`. `thirtyDays` remains in `impl.go:25`, and there is a local `thirtyDays` in `pkg/api/admin.go:67`. The rename in `api.go` unified the name in one file only; exporting a single constant from `anonstore` would remove the drift.

findings.title: `updateDevice` doc comment does not match its signature
findings.description: The comment says the device is updated if it "has been updated between the given times", but the function takes no time arguments; the window is derived from `device.UpdatedAt`. The comment also omits that a no-match returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: Settings refactor and DTO plumbing
findings.description: Extracting `anonSection` is a behaviour-preserving cleanup, and `MustInt64(0)` gives a safe "disabled" default. The field is passed through `FrontendSettingsDTO` and `getFrontendSettings` consistently with the neighbouring `AnonymousEnabled` field.
